_schema.what: The G-ADDR (dial ADDRESSABILITY) floor registry. One committed row per (instrument, REFERENCE), holding that reference scorer's measured end-of-range behaviour on that instrument. A candidate bake clears the REGRESSION tier only when it reaches at least as far at BOTH ends as the ACTIVE reference's row for the instrument it was measured on.
_schema.why: USER RULE 2026-09-04: 'floor and ceiling dial addressability is crucial ... any model that limits dial range cannot ship'. A dial that compresses at the ends cannot serve a target near the ends, which is where near-lossless product decisions live. SROCC is rank-invariant and structurally cannot see this; G1 (p5<=25, p95>=85) is far too loose to.
_schema.keyed_by: (dial_grid_sha256, reference) for the grid rows; (probe_sha256, reference) for the negative-tail and identity rows. BOTH halves are load-bearing: a row is a measurement OF ONE SCORER on one instrument, so reading a peer_ssim2 bar off a shipped_b row would compare a candidate against the wrong mentor. An UNREGISTERED grid or probe is NOT-MEASURABLE / NOT-MEASURED, never a pass -- a bar you can dodge by choosing a friendlier instrument is not a bar.

reference_sets.ACTIVE (bars): peer_ssim2 -- the REFERENCE METRIC. USER DECISION 2026-09-04, verbatim: 'I don't think we should pin to B, ssim2 seems a better mentor.' Direction semantics: a candidate must address AT LEAST the range ssim2 addresses (reach/max/p95/DR/frac<0 >= ssim2's; min/p5/negtail-min/negtail-p1 <= ssim2's).
reference_sets.incumbent (printed, never a bar): shipped_b -- the shipped product dial. Retained so a reader can always see whether a fail is 'worse than the mentor' or 'worse than what shipped', and so the pre-2026-09-04 verdicts stay readable against the pins they were graded on. Labelled BIASED: measured on 2026-09-04 to put A1/A3/A6 ABOVE the reference metric's own values on the same grid (bars 99.98/99.72/86.08 vs truth 98.38/95.46/85.20 -- a dial calibrated exactly to the truth failed all three, and so did both other shipped profiles), and to meet A4 (p5 <= 13.65) only through a -23-point low-band bias (B reads +11.97 on the 221 lowest-truth cells where the truth is -11.30; the train-on-test ORACLE, the ceiling for any monotone re-map of B's ordering, reads p5 21.5-22.8).
reference_sets.not a relaxation: Re-pinning MOVED the difficulty from the ceiling to the FLOOR. ssim2's grid min is -55.35 against B's +3.13 and its negative-tail probe is 100% below zero against B's 0%, so A2/A5/A7-A9 all got much harder. That is correct: the floor is where the incumbent is genuinely broken.
reference_sets.rows without a `reference` field: pre-2026-09-04 rows, all shipped_b. A serde default supplies the label so those rows stay BYTE-UNTOUCHED, which is what append-only requires.
reference_sets.derivation: Every peer_ssim2 value came out of the owner instrument at full f64 precision -- `bake_verdict --dial-peer-scores peer_ssim2=<cells> --negtail-peer-scores ... --identity-peer-scores ... --gaddr-json` -- never from percentile math re-implemented beside it.

_schema.owner: zensim-validate/src/dial_addressability.rs (embedded with include_str!, so a stale or missing file cannot silently disarm the gate). Consumed by bake_verdict's DIAL panel; emitted into --full-json at dial.addressability.
_schema.two_tiers: REGRESSION rows (A*) bar against the ACTIVE reference's value on the same instrument -- since 2026-09-04, 'addresses at least the range ssim2 addresses'. CONTRACT rows (C*) are absolute product requirements. The shipped dial FAILS four contract rows today (C3/C4 negative tail, C5 identity band, C6 nothing-above-identity); those are standing defects recorded here, NOT bars invented for this gate, and the `incumbent` column in every report says so. MEASURED 2026-09-04: peer_ssim2 PASSES all six contract rows -- mono 0.9924, tied 0.0000, negtail frac<0 1.0000 / min -770.62, identity exactly 100.0000 on all 38 refs, 0 of 4,424 cells above identity. That is what 'as good as the mentor at the ends' means, and it is a measurement, not a target.
_schema.append_only: Rows are appended, never edited. A floor is a measurement of a specific bake on a specific instrument; changing it retroactively invalidates every verdict that quoted it. To raise a bar (a better dial ships), append a new row and retire the old one by label.

negative_tail_bars._what: The NEGATIVE-TAIL / FLOOR rows of G-ADDR. Two pin sets, both kept: `mentor-2026-09-04` (RETIRED) barred rows A7/A8/A9 against `peer_ssim2`'s own measured DEPTH on one probe; `floor-representability-2026-09-05` (ACTIVE, OPERATIVE) asks instead whether each codec's LOWEST CONFIGURABLE SETTINGS still resolve, and contains NO dial-value bar of any kind. Selected at run time by `bake_verdict --gaddr-tail-pins {product|retired}`; the default is the active set. A1-A6 are untouched by this and remain mentor-pinned.
negative_tail_bars.user_ruling_2026-09-05_first: the negative tail bar is entirely arbitrary. below -5-50
negative_tail_bars.user_ruling_2026-09-05_correction: i said -50 not -5, codecs are all different, some go lower than others
negative_tail_bars.user_ruling_2026-09-05_final_OPERATIVE: i care that the lowest configurable settings per codec are representable, not that negative fifty is in that specifically
negative_tail_bars._which_is_in_force: The THIRD form is OPERATIVE. The first two are recorded because they are the sequence the rule was arrived at and because the intermediate reading briefly landed in this file, but NEITHER -5 NOR -50 IS A BAR ANYWHERE in the active pin set. The only numbers the active rule carries are `bottom_k` (how many of a codec's lowest settings must resolve) and `clamp_eps` (float tolerance for 'sitting on the clamp'); the per-codec BAR is the reference metric's own measured fraction on the same cells.
negative_tail_bars._ruling_reading: A dial serves a codec's low end when the codec's lowest configurable settings are still DISTINGUISHABLE on it. Depth is not the question - a dial could reach -700 and still be useless at the bottom if its three lowest steps tie or invert, and a dial that stops at -12 is fine if every step still resolves. So: for each `(image_id, codec)` ladder on the canonical dial grid (REAL CODEC OUTPUT), take the `bottom_k` lowest configurable settings - the lowest q steps; for JXL the largest distances, which the grid stores as its lowest `q`, so 'lowest q' is correct on every codec - and require (i) the dial strictly increases across those steps AND into the next step up (no ties, no inversions), and (ii) no bottom step sits within `clamp_eps` of the dial's instrument-wide minimum, UNLESS that ladder is the SINGLE ladder attaining the minimum. Somebody has to be lowest; two or more ladders sharing the bottom value is a floor that has collapsed onto a clamp, and neither ladder is addressable there.
negative_tail_bars._scope: The ruling is about the REGRESSION tail. NO contract row was added, removed or moved, so the CONTRACT tier -- and therefore the board's NOT SHIPPABLE badge, which is contract-driven -- is unaffected. C3 ('some row of an all-negative-truth probe scores < 0') and C4 ('the deepest probe dial is below 0') keep their absolute 0.0 bars, which are SIGN requirements, not depth bars.

pin_sets.retired_by: USER RULING 2026-09-05. Asked "ok, is there poor resolution compared to ssim2?", the lane reported that this set's `distinct` window grades each ladder's three literal lowest positions -- including steps the MENTOR itself cannot resolve -- and recommended grading only the steps ssim2 separates by >= 0.5 points. The user answered "ok", read as accepting that recommendation. Superseded by `floor-representability-resolvable-2026-09-05`.
pin_sets.retained_because: Every A7r number published between 2026-09-05 and this flip -- gate record section 16, the 11-arm lambda sweep table, the 2026-09-05 board grading -- is graded on THIS set's `distinct` window. Reachable with `--floor-rule distinct`, or by pointing `negative_tail_bars.active` back here (no code change).

axis_definitions.A7r: FLOOR REPRESENTABILITY, per codec, on the canonical dial grid (real codec output). Fraction of that codec's `(image_id, codec)` ladders whose `bottom_k` lowest configurable settings are REPRESENTED: (i) the dial strictly increases across those steps and into the next one up, and (ii) none of them sits within `clamp_eps` of the dial's instrument-wide minimum, unless that ladder is the sole holder of the minimum. BAR = the REFERENCE metric's own fraction on the same cells, pinned per codec in `grid_floor_representability`; the incumbent's fraction is printed beside it. The row's `measured` value is the COUNT of codecs below their mentor bar, barred at <= 0. A codec on which the mentor itself represents nothing gets a bar of 0.0 -- the natural analogue of an exemption, needing no special case.
axis_definitions.A8r: The negative-tail probe, REPORT-ONLY on tier `report-only` (excluded from both tier verdicts by construction). Pooled `min` and `p1` are printed with the probe's own reference-truth extremes; NOTHING is barred. Reason: the probe carries no codec identity at all -- its rows are KADIS distortion types, not codec output -- so it cannot answer the ruling's question. Its per-DISTORTION-family reading is measured in benchmarks/d_peaks_lambda_sweep_2026-09-05.md sections 4-6, where grading it at a fixed depth was shown to fail every bake ever built on one n=8 family.

dropped_axes.A9r: DROPPED as a bar. Its per-codec quantity -- of a codec's cells whose reference truth is at or below `report_floor_threshold`, the fraction the dial also places at or below it -- is FOLDED INTO the per-codec report block as the `ref<=floor also dial<=floor` column. `report_floor_threshold` is a REPORTING threshold for that one column and is barred against NOTHING; it is the only place -50 survives in this file, and it survives as information.

provenance.bottom_k: user-ruling, verbatim: "the lowest K=3 configurable settings present in the grid for that codec"
provenance.clamp_eps: user-ruling, verbatim: "a value equal (within 1e-9) to the dial's instrument-wide minimum counts as clamped"
provenance.sole_holder_exception: user-ruling, verbatim: "unless that ladder is the single ladder attaining the minimum (two or more ladders sharing the bottom value = a collapsed floor)"
provenance.per_codec_bars: MEASURED, not chosen: each codec's bar is `peer_ssim2`'s own representability fraction on the same cells, derived through the owner instrument (`bake_verdict --dial-peer-scores peer_ssim2=<cells> --gaddr-json`) and appended to `grid_floor_representability`. Re-implementing the ladder walk outside the owner to produce these would be exactly the duplication the no-duplicate-implementations rule forbids.

pin_sets.quality_orientation: `q` is QUALITY-ORIENTED on every codec in the dial grid, including JXL: its `param_kind` is `distance` and its q=0 cells carry `codec_param` 25.0 (the largest distance = the worst quality), rising to q=99.8 at distance 0.05. So 'the lowest configurable settings' is always the smallest `q`, and no per-codec direction switch is needed. VERIFIED 2026-09-05 on the canonical grid: avif/jpeg/webp q in [0,100] with codec_param == q, jxl q in [0,99.8] with codec_param 25.0 -> 0.05 monotonically decreasing.

user_messages_verbatim_2026-09-05: ok, is there poor resolution compared to ssim2? update and share thw gauntlet for what should be the. ew sdr and bdr
pin_sets._ruling_reading: The two messages are one instruction: the second supplies the word the first mistyped, so the ask is "update and share the gauntlet for what should be the new SDR and HDR [defaults]". The leading "ok" answers the two recommendations the previous report put to the user, and IS READ AS ACCEPTING BOTH: (1) grade floor representability under the RESOLVABLE window (margin 0.5) instead of the literal bottom-3 window, and (2) demote the six dial-VALUE rows A1-A6 from hard regression bars to the Report tier. This reading is recorded explicitly because "ok" is terse: it is an INFERENCE from the conversation, not a verbatim instruction, and both halves are reversible without a code change -- point `active` back at `floor-representability-2026-09-05` for the window, pass `--gaddr-value-pins hard` for the tier.

axis_definitions.A7r: FLOOR REPRESENTABILITY, per codec, under the RESOLVABLE window. Identical to the superseded set's rule -- a ladder is REPRESENTED when the dial strictly increases across the selected steps and into the next one up, and no bottom step sits within `clamp_eps` of the instrument-wide minimum unless that ladder is its sole holder -- EXCEPT in which steps it selects. `distinct` took each ladder's literal three lowest settings; `resolvable` walks up from the lowest setting, SKIPPING any step whose |delta mentor| from the last SELECTED step is below `floor_margin`, until bottom_k+1 mentor-resolvable steps are collected. BAR = the reference metric's own fraction on the same cells under the SAME rule, pinned per codec in `grid_floor_representability` rows carrying `"floor_rule": "resolvable"`; where no such row is registered the bar is computed LIVE through the identical owner call. A `distinct` fraction is NEVER substituted for a `resolvable` one.
axis_definitions.A8r: Unchanged from the superseded set: the negative-tail probe, REPORT-ONLY, no bar.

pin_sets.why_resolvable: MEASURED, `benchmarks/ladder_floor_resolution_2026-09-05.md` sections 2-4 and 8.3. The `distinct` window grades steps the MENTOR itself cannot separate, so it charges a candidate for disagreeing with noise. The extreme case is jpeg on the pre-ladder grids, where q=0/5/10 are BYTE-IDENTICAL encoder output and the bar was a vacuous 0.0000; the ladder instrument fixed the instrument, and this rule fixes the WINDOW. On the ladder instrument the mentor's own bottom-triplet failures are 78% (jpeg) / 67% (avif-rav1e) genuine inversions rather than ties, so the flat zone is real and skipping it is not hiding a defect -- it is declining to grade where the reference cannot.

value_pins._what: Which tier the six dial-VALUE rows A1-A6 are emitted on. `report` is the default from 2026-09-05: they are still MEASURED and still PRINTED with their bars, but sit on tier `report-only` and gate nothing, so the REGRESSION headline is carried by A7r alone. `--gaddr-value-pins hard` restores them to the regression tier and reproduces the pre-ruling grading row-for-row.
value_pins.why: A1-A6 bar a candidate against `peer_ssim2`'s own max / p95 / min / p5 / reach / dynamic_range on one instrument. Those are incidental properties of where the mentor's distribution happens to land, not product requirements -- and the gate record's own section 14.6 measured the resulting absurdity under the RETIRED shipped-B pins, where A1/A3/A6 sat ABOVE what the reference metric itself reaches, so a dial calibrated exactly to the truth failed three rows. The product requirements live in the CONTRACT tier (C1-C6) and the per-codec floor (A7r).
value_pins.scope: TIER ONLY. No contract row was added, removed, moved or re-barred, so the board's NOT SHIPPABLE badge -- which is contract-driven -- cannot move with this setting. Asserted by a unit test, not assumed.

pin_sets.reversibility: Two independent levers, neither requiring a code change: point `negative_tail_bars.active` back at `floor-representability-2026-09-05` to restore the `distinct` window everywhere, or pass `--floor-rule distinct` / `--gaddr-value-pins hard` per invocation.
pin_sets.not_measurable_note: `resolvable` chooses each ladder's window from the MENTOR's own per-cell values, so it REQUIRES `--gaddr-grid-truth`. Where none is supplied A7r reads NOT MEASURED with that reason -- it is never silently re-graded under `distinct`'s window, which asks a different question, and never defaulted to a pass.

inversion_truth._what: The two-reference INVERSION-ATTRIBUTION rule. A material backwards rung on a dial ladder is charged to the ENCODER, and leaves the dial's `mono` (hence C1) and the zone census, only where BOTH reference metrics independently say the higher setting is worse by a material margin. Everything else stays the dial's, INCLUDING every pair whose attribution cannot be decided.
inversion_truth._user_ruling_2026_09_05_verbatim: for inversions, we should choose say ssim2 and butter and only flag true inversions where they agree, and we can then file or update tracking issues on codecs for when they are nonmonotonic.
inversion_truth.owner: zensim_validate::dial_addressability::encoder_inversion — ONE function, shared by the G-ADDR contract's `mono` input and bake_verdict's ladder-inversion census, so the gate and the census cannot drift apart on what an encoder inversion is.
inversion_truth.legacy_reading: single — every material backwards rung charged to the dial. Retained and selectable (`bake_verdict --inversion-truth single`) so every number published before 2026-09-05 stays reproducible. MEASURED: a `single` run is byte-identical to the pre-ruling binary (0 JSON differences on shipped Profile D over the 9,593-row ladder instrument).

margins.ssim2_derivation: NOT re-derived — this is bake_verdict's own MATERIAL_INV_PT, so the reference is held to exactly the bar the dial is held to.
margins.butteraugli_derivation: p85 of |delta variant| over FORWARD adjacent pairs whose delta-ssim2 lies in [0.45, 0.55] — the moves ssim2 itself calls exactly material — rounded UP to the next 0.05. MEASURED on the 2026-09-05 ladder instrument (n=410 in band): pnorm3 p25/med/p75/p85 = 0.0238/0.0315/0.0403/0.0481 -> 0.05; max = 0.0037/0.0677/0.1361/0.2189 -> 0.25. Stable to +/-0.0007 across the wider bands [0.4,0.6] and [0.25,0.75], so it is not band-choice.
margins.why_not_a_noise_margin: There is no measurement noise to derive one from. MEASURED: re-running the instrument's jpeg leg from scratch reproduces 2,574/2,574 cells with max|delta| = 0 on BOTH butteraugli variants (as well as ssim2, dssim and encoded bytes) — extending the instrument's own reproducibility gate, which checked only bytes and ssim2. A reproducibility-derived margin would be 0.0, which is not a materiality bar.
margins.rounding_direction: UP, deliberately. A LARGER butteraugli margin makes agreement RARER, so fewer inversions are excused and MORE stay charged to the dial. The ruling cannot launder a dial defect by being generous with this number.

inversion_truth.variant_evidence: MEASURED over all 9,411 adjacent distinct pairs of the ladder instrument, the share on which the variant moves the direction ssim2 moves: pnorm3 94.30 %, max 75.27 %. In the population where ssim2 barely moves (|delta| < 0.05), max's own p95 excursion is 1.27 against pnorm3's 0.14. `max` is reported BESIDE pnorm3, never instead of it.
inversion_truth.unknown_is_not_an_exemption: A pair whose reference values are not both on disk is NOT MEASURABLE and stays charged to the DIAL. bake_verdict counts and reports those pairs (`dial.inversion_truth.n_attribution_unknown`), and a requested `agree` with no usable reference table degrades to `single` LOUDLY, never silently.
inversion_truth.c1_direction_property: mono_agree = 1 - dial/pairs and mono_single = 1 - (dial+encoder)/pairs, so mono_agree >= mono_single for every non-negative encoder count. C1 is a `>=` bar on mono and is mono's ONLY gate consumer, so the ruling can move C1 up and never down. Gate: dial_addressability::tests::encoder_attribution_moves_c1_up_and_never_down.

reference_tables.note: the SECONDARY variant, reported beside pnorm3

reference_tables.grid: dial_grid_944col_ladder.parquet — the SAME 9,593 cells at 944 width, so the same reference tables serve it

inversion_truth.not_measurable_on: Every dial grid built before the 2026-09-05 ladder instrument. MEASURED: the canonical 372 grid and the 944 POOLS grid carry ssim2 per-cell tables but the ONLY butteraugli on disk for them is `dialcells_butteraugli_944grid.tsv`, whose variant the artifact does not name. Identified empirically as `max` (median relative error 0.0029 against score_butteraugli_max over 4,105 independently-encoded cells, against 0.58 for pnorm3) — so the PRIMARY variant does not exist for those cells, and re-scoring it is not honestly possible because the pixels that produced them are a different decoder/encoder generation. Those grids therefore read `single` with the loud NOT MEASURABLE note.
